BFM practice 2v2 · 22:38Z

Virtual Egyptian Air Force · 2026-11-27 · AI-assisted debrief · approved by Sword
TRAININGBFMA-ABVR

Instructor narrative

This was an extended BFM and 1v1/2v1 PVP training session on the Sinai map, running 27 rounds over approximately two hours of continuous BFM action. MeGaTron dominated the first half of the session against Omar, winning 9 of 12 solo rounds with consistent offensive conversions — his ability to get to the bandit's six and stay there is clearly improving from prior sorties. The standout tactical moment was Round 5, where MeGaTron held a 47-second gun saddle and fired 77 rounds; the problem is none connected, which is the defining weakness of his BFM game this session. Omar, by contrast, spent nearly every engagement entirely defensive or cold, achieving 0% offensive time in nine of fifteen solo rounds — he is not yet converting the merge into an offensive opportunity. However, Omar's persistence across fifteen contested engagements against a pilot who consistently outpoints him demonstrates exactly the attitude that builds proficiency over time, and the instructor has directed that persistence be credited accordingly. When Sword entered at Round 10, he immediately showed his more experienced pedigree — a patient 259-second engagement ending with a close-range AIM-9 kill after 248 seconds of positioning, which is the correct use of a short-range IR missile inside 1 nm. The subsequent 2v1 (Round 13, 645 s) saw Sword and Omar combine to press MeGaTron, ultimately with Sword delivering the kill — the longest and most tactically complex round of the session. The Borhms-vs-Sword series from Rounds 19–27 was competitive and revealing: Borhms' aggressive offensive game won four of the first six bouts, but Sword reversed the trend in Rounds 26 and 27 with better energy management. Gun accuracy remains zero across all pilots this session — a systemic issue that must be addressed before the next BFM block. No friendly kills, no deck or landing penalties applied per instructor directive.
  • Gun discipline: every pilot fired hundreds of rounds and scored zero hits. The common failure is pulling the trigger from the saddle before achieving proper lead picture — mandatory dry-fire trigger discipline drill (wait for the pipper to stabilise on the target silhouette for ≥0.5 s before firing) must precede the next live BFM block.
  • Merge energy management: multiple pilots (MeGaTron in Round 10, Sword in Rounds 19–22, Borhms in the Sword series) arrived at the merge with below-corner airspeed and immediately ceded the offensive — brief the entry airspeed and altitude band before each round (530–580 kt at 8,000–10,000 ft for the F-16 BFM arena) and enforce it.
  • Offensive initiation for defensive pilots (Omar): spending 80–100% of time cold or neutral is not 'surviving' — it is losing slowly. Omar must be given a specific task each round: 'your job is to achieve at least 15 seconds offensive time before the round ends.' Measure and brief this metric each debrief.

Pilot evaluations

C

Omar

65 pts
bfm_win_rate 5 · bfm_offensive_efficiency 5 · bfm_gun_discipline 5 · bfm_persistence_bonus 15 · participation_base 10 · flight_time_credit 5 · landing_quality 0 · airmanship_general 10 · formation_discipline 10
+ Showed up for every round — 15 BFM engagements against MeGaTron plus rounds 13/16 in multi-ship: total BFM flight time across all slots exceeds 60 min of actual airtime, demonstrating outstanding persistence and commitment to learning.
+ Round 15 (400 s, merge at 9,117 ft/625 kt): went 16% offensive with 70 s offensive time and fired gun on the merge — showed the most aggressive posture of the session with 3 g of deck busts, indicating willingness to press low; round survived without a death, an improvement.
− Offensive percentage was 0% in 9 of 15 solo rounds — Omar is spending almost all time in neutral or cold, never finding a firing solution. Must practise the initial turn fight: get to the bandit's 6 o'clock within the first 60 s.
− AIM-9 employment: 0 hits from roughly 20 missiles fired (all rounds combined). Shots are going off-boresight ('Unknown' target on most) indicating no tone before trigger pull — wait for growl and sight picture before firing.
Airmanship: Landing at Jiyanklis graded F (score 45): AoA 7.7° against 13° target, speed SD 8.3 kt, sink rate 2,192 fpm below 500 ft, bounced, 14.3 m off centreline. Per instructor directive landing/over-G penalties are waived. Taxi overspeed 7 s at peak 31 kt — minor note only. Formation bracket recorded (round 15 slot): 100% outside — Omar was never in position when formation data was sampled. Formation discipline score 0 for the one measurable session. Despite the losses, the attitude shown by returning for every round is exactly what this programme needs; score reflects persistence credit as directed.

82 pts
bfm_win_rate 25 · bfm_offensive_efficiency 13 · bfm_gun_discipline 8 · bfm_persistence_bonus 10 · participation_base 10 · flight_time_credit 5 · landing_quality 0 · airmanship_general 7 · formation_discipline 4
+ Dominant BFM record vs Omar across 12 solo rounds (9W–1L–2D in rounds 1-12/14-15): maintained offensive pressure and converted gun saddles consistently, averaging ~40 s offensive time per engagement.
+ Round 5 gunfight: achieved 47 s saddle time and fired 77 rounds at merge alt ~9,000 ft — textbook conversion from corner speed to sustained gun track.
− Gun accuracy was 0% across all rounds despite hundreds of rounds fired; saddle time is not translating to hits — trigger discipline and lead computation need dedicated dry-fire review.
− Round 10 loss to Sword (259 s, 54 s defensive, only 2 s offensive): failed to handle the 1v1 role reversal — energy got down to 169 kt min recorded, spent 18 s energy-poor. Must maintain airspeed discipline when switching opponents.
Airmanship: Max G peaked at 11.8 g in round 15 — well above structural limit; however per instructor directive over-G is not penalised this sortie. Deck busts noted across multiple rounds (up to 4 per round) but also waived. Instructor should note recurring energy poverty (up to 30 s per slot) indicating MeGaTron is bleeding airspeed in the vertical and not trading altitude for speed effectively. Formation data sparse (BFM spawn environment).

Sword

78 pts
bfm_win_rate 20 · bfm_offensive_efficiency 12 · bfm_gun_discipline 9 · bfm_persistence_bonus 8 · participation_base 10 · flight_time_credit 5 · landing_quality 0 · airmanship_general 7 · formation_discipline 7
+ Beat MeGaTron in Round 10 (259 s, AIM-9 splash at 0.9 nm for a PK=100% kill) after 248 s of patience — excellent range discipline on the shot, waited until inside 1 nm before triggering.
+ Beat Borhms in Round 27 (273 s, 48 s offensive, 14 s saddle, gun kill) demonstrating that when energy is managed correctly Sword can dominate the prolonged turning fight.
− Rounds 19–25 vs Borhms: went 0–4 before reversing — Sword was consistently losing the first 90 s of each fight, spending 68% of time defensive. Entry to the merge needs work: Sword arrived low-energy (min 80 kt in round 22 slot) and immediately ceded the offensive.
− Max G hit 12.9 g in round 27 — far above the F-16 9 g structural limit. Even waived for scoring, repeated over-limit pulls risk in-game system failures and train bad habits; must learn to cap pull at corner speed.
Airmanship: Recorded max G of 12.9 g in one slot — the highest of any pilot this session. Energy-poor time was significant (up to 139 s in round 26 slot), indicating Sword sometimes runs out of airspeed in extended turning fights and relies on the other pilot also being slow. Round 13 (645 s 2v1): Sword performed the missile kill on MeGaTron (AIM-9 splash at 0.9 nm) after a lengthy coordinated engagement — shows BVR situational awareness even inside visual range. No formation data to assess (BFM arena spawns). Trend from history (90→82→78) is a slight decline — needs to sharpen energy management.

Landings

Every landing on a runway DCS knows. Touchdown: distance past the threshold (150-600 m is the zone), offset from the centreline (+ right), track against the runway. Sink at touchdown, ground speed, AoA corrected for wind (on-speed target in brackets: F/A-18C 8.1°, F-16C 13°), wind/crosswind (kt, + from the right). Approach from 500 to 50 ft: speed spread, average glidepath error against 3°, worst sink. Rollout / runway left when below 30 kt. Score: 100 less deductions (zone, centreline, alignment, crab, bounces, AoA, approach, damage), times 1.0/0.9/0.7/0.4 for touchdown sink up to 300/600/900/over 900 fpm. A 90+, B 80+, C 70+, D 60+.
